text:
Late morning and the day is playing out just the way the high pressure promised: sunshine from edge to edge, calm air, and a climb from a frosty start into the mid 40s already. We'll keep warming through the afternoon and top out right around 56, with a few spots flirting with 60. That's a touch above normal for late October, and with no wind to speak of, it'll feel even nicer in the sun. The sun sets just before 6, so the best window for a walk or a look at the last of the foliage is from noon to about 4.

Tonight stays clear and quiet, and cold again. The forecasters have a low around 35, but calm, clear nights tend to overachieve, so I'd expect frost on the windshield and cover anything tender outside.

Sunday is the warmer day, sunny with a high near 61 and a light south breeze by afternoon. Some models run a few degrees warmer, so low 60s is a fair bet. A cold front Monday might bring a sprinkle, but the air is so dry I'd leave the umbrella home. Tuesday is the noticeably cooler day, with highs struggling into the mid 40s.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-24T11:06:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Beautiful weekend on tap for the North Country.
  2. Cold front on Monday may bring a few showers but dry weather is largely expected through the upcoming week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 212 AM EDT Saturday... No significant changes have been made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: There may be a few high clouds present at sunrise but sunny skies will prevail both today and Sunday. A 1033 mb high pressure has become well established across the region this morning and will remain in place through much of the day Sunday. As a result, winds will be light and variable throughout the day today. Winds will shift to the south at 7-12 mph Sunday afternoon as this high departs to the east and gradient flow begins to pick up. No precipitation is expected this weekend as high temperatures will be near or slightly above seasonal normals. KEY MESSAGE 2: A cold front is slated to move across the region during the second half of Monday. There are an increasing number of deterministic models and ensemble perturbations that are showing increasing rain chances Monday afternoon and evening across parts of the forecast area. However, the consensus is still favoring a mostly dry passage of the cold front. We have introduced some 20-30 PoPs for portions of northern New York and northern Vermont as a result but the antecedent dry air will likely make it very difficult for any rain to make it to the surface. Thereafter, temperatures on Tuesday will be noticeably cooler as highs will struggle to warm into the mid 40s. Another high pressure system, this one even stronger than the last, will move overhead on Wednesday which will allow the extended period of dry weather to continue. Temperatures will also moderate underneath this high pressure system with temps clicking back into the upper 40s to mid 50s on Wednesday. There is a chance we could see a frontal boundary approach from the west late next week but looks rather unimpressive at this time.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - The continued dry but pleasant weather will continue over the weekend. It was a cold morning with temperatures in the 20s, but the afternoon will be sunny and warmer with highs in the 50s. A few spots could hit 60 degrees. Sunday will continue the sunny skies with pleasant highs in the mid-50s to low 60s. The fall foliage is now past peak throughout the region, but some trees still have color, so the weekend will be great for viewing any remaining foliage. Overall, the week will remain dry, but the fire danger will remain relatively low due to a lack of wind. A cold front will come through on Monday. An isolated shower is possible, but most of the region is expected to remain dry. Highs will be in the 50s to around 60 degrees. The front will, however, usher in colder air for Tuesday. Despite mostly sunny skies, it will be chilly with highs in the 40s. Lows will be in the 20s, though some teens are expected. Wednesday and Thursday will be mostly sunny. Highs will be near 50 degrees on Wednesday, but Thursday’s highs will be closer to 60 degrees. Another system may bring a higher chance for showers on Friday, but no significant rain is in the forecast.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-24T11:50:00Z — same caveat): Lots of sunshine, turning a bit milder Saturday — After a widespread hard freeze, expect a nice temperature rebound through Saturday. Highs reach the 50s to near 60. Besides a few morning clouds and patchy fog, expect nearly full sunshine. Tonight will again be quite cold, due to clear skies and light wind. Temperatures fall back to the 20s and low 30s. Expect another round of frost and freeze conditions. High pressure stays nearby Sunday, bringing full sunshine! It turns warmer, thanks to a light south breeze that develops. Highs reach the mid-60s. An approaching cold front brings more clouds and a few spot showers for northern areas on Monday. Southern Vermont looks brighter overall. Highs will be near 60. Behind that front, a shot of unseasonable cold arrives Tuesday, as highs fall back to the mid-40s. Expect a mix of sun and clouds. Wednesday stays cool, with highs near 50 and a partly sunny sky. Another warmup arrives late week with highs near 60, thanks to a gusty south breeze. A few showers are likely later Thursday into Friday, with another cold front on approach, though not anticipating any significant rain. Halloween weekend looks dry and seasonable, with partly sunny skies. Highs reach the mid and upper 50s.
